title: Playing around town and the end of the Louisiana Shakers
summary: On returning he freelanced; he had a band with Howard in the 1930s that folded after Handy left for St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, when you stopped your business in Pastor Christian and came over here, who did you play with?
All different fellas. I never had no particular one to play with. Just afternoon I was in town. He called me up, asked me to work and I'd accept the job.
Never worked with Ken Howland? Oh yeah, Howland and I had a band together.
Oh that was back in the 30s.
Yeah we had a band together.
As a matter of fact I tried to get Howard to keep the band going when I went to St. Louis. He said he was but business run out on him I suppose. Because I was getting most of the work.
Now who took your place in that band when you left for St. Louis?

I don't know. That's something I never did find out. Because I don't think it stayed together much longer after I left. Because I was doing all the booking and that's what was keeping the band together. See some work if you didn't have no work you couldn't keep the band together. So I was doing all the booking. When I left they had to stop the booking see. So I didn't do much playing. Of course Howard had a few jobs. And they didn't want a big band because I had 10, 11, or 12 pieces in my band. At that time they just wanted to. Howard was getting a lot of six piece jobs. You know how long that's going to keep the big band together. Take the six out of the playing. First opportunity they got to join another band they just left.
So that was the end of the Louisiana Shakers. So when did you come back to town from Paschristown? What year was that?
Oh I don't know exactly when I left Paschristown and come back here.
Was that during World War II or after? No no. After? Before? World War II I was in Paschristown then.
And I don't remember what year I left there and come back over here. But I was there in World War II alone.
I'm trying to remember some of the different people I heard you with you know. Since 1949 like Howard, Annie Williams some.
